extracted.title: Beheading Hydras: Performing Effective Botnet Takedowns
extracted.venue: ACM CCS 2013 (peer reviewed), 4 to 8 November 2013; copy read from the authors' institution
extracted.licence_statement_found: ACM notice permits personal or classroom copies; republishing or redistribution requires permission: not a licence allowing redistribution
extracted.inclusion: included (Part A): botnet takedowns (domain seizure and sinkholing); outcome is successful DNS lookups to the takedown's domains and to related infrastructure, 14 days around each takedown; method stated
extracted.population: aggregate daily successful DNS resolutions at one large North American ISP's passive DNS (appendix repeats with another passive DNS source); three takedowns dated 26 September 2011, 25 March 2012 and 11 September 2012; 45 active botnets for the recommendation analysis
extracted.data_public: no: ISP passive DNS; one author's employer a security company tracking the 45 botnets
outcome_facts: First takedown (late 2011): "The day Kelihos was taken down, we see lookups to the seed domains completely stop"; the authors judge it "largely a success" and add that new variants "emerged soon after" (not measured in their data)
Second takedown (March 2012): lookups to sinkholed domains dropped; improvement ratios indicate related malicious domains were left untouched

Third takedown (September 2012): "We notice a drop in lookups" to malware-associated and low-reputation domains, "however, the lookups to remaining infrastructure identified by rza are still frequent"
Recommendation analysis: "42 of them can likely be disabled entirely by using a DNS-based takedown strategy only" (of 45 active botnets; a system estimate)
